acceptanceCriteria: A Git call that exits 0 while its output reader is starved for several seconds returns its output instead of a WaitDelay failure.
A descendant that keeps Git's output open still fails the call within a bounded time, and a test pins both cases.
A signal-killed or pipe-drain failure is reported as such, not as "returned non-zero exit status -1".
body: internal/contextindex/process_unix.go:25 (and process_other.go, process_windows.go) sets command.WaitDelay = time.Second. os/exec starts that timer when Git exits, so if the goroutine copying stdout into boundedBuffer is not scheduled within one second, Wait returns exec.ErrWaitDelay although Git succeeded. On a starved host (load 400-650, swap full) this turns successful Git calls into failures: 37 contextindex test failures were WaitDelay only and pass on single rerun, and the c-flakes dogfood-change local-outcome step failed twice with record-failed. tracerecordrepo recordIndexError (adapter.go:604-627) then renders the empty-stderr, exit -1 failure as "repository changed while reading local traces: ... returned non-zero exit status -1", which names neither the signal nor the pipe drain. worksource/git.go:157 (one minute) and cem/gitrun pipeDrainDelay already treat the drain bound as a hang detector held in a variable that tests shorten; gokernel, doccompiler, taskman and liveverify/mutate still use one second.

completion.reason: Fixed in cb7644b2, 0cafa867 and 7de563e0 (pipe-drain bound is a hang detector, PR 273). Contained in the 1.0.0-rc.1 candidate 94ca556f52c0349c0a48e0c3a3274f8a0b5e6db3 on origin/main. Owner-approved closure 2026-09-27.

title: A one-second pipe-drain bound fails successful Git calls on a loaded host
